description: The Ocneanu parameter N is the quantum dimension of the fibre, not a free knob: sum_lambda f^lambda s_lambda(1,q,..,q^{N-1}) = [N]_q^n, the categorical trace of the identity on V^(tensor n). Resolves T3f's 'Unknown' for the mass channel. Beans qou-w5fw, qou-8p1x.

computation.arithmetic: exact Fraction; hook-length + q-hook-content; no floats

data.provenance: dual Cauchy identity p_1^n = sum_lambda f^lambda s_lambda, evaluated at the principal specialisation where p_1 = [N]_q
data.reading: [N]_q is the quantum dimension of an N-dimensional fibre, so the total Ocneanu weight at parameter N is the categorical trace of the identity on V^(tensor n) with dim_q V = [N]_q; choosing N is choosing V
data.corpus_basis: feynman-eigenbasis.md defines the mass as the categorical trace summed over irreducible summands of V^(tensor n), and quotes the skein relation at a = q (i.e. a = q^{N-1} with N = 2)
data.verdict: the mass channel is N = 2 because the Descartes condition fixes dim V = 2 and the categorical trace's parameter is slaved to the fibre's quantum dimension; T3f's 'Unknown' is resolved for the mass channel
data.sharpens_flavour: an N = 3 flavour channel cannot be the same trace re-tuned (lock-in probe) and by this identity must be the categorical trace on a genuinely 3-dimensional object -- the same missing 3-dim fibre qou-8p1x identifies. The Ocneanu route restates the need for a 3-dim fibre rather than avoiding it
not_claimed: that the Descartes condition is itself derived -- it is an input
that no other trace could serve the mass pipeline; the claim is conditional on the corpus's own definition of mass as a categorical trace on V^(tensor n)
